name: Louis de Broglie
affiliation: Faculty of Sciences, University of Paris
role: Gave the report on the new dynamics of quanta, presenting the pilot-wave theory
bio: A historian by first training and a prince by birth, de Broglie proposed in his 1924 thesis that waves accompany all particles. Einstein read it and called attention to it; Schrödinger built wave mechanics on it; in 1927 Davisson and Germer, and G. P. Thomson, diffracted electrons. At this council he presents a causal theory in which a real particle is guided by a real wave — the first worked-out alternative to the statistical view. It is received coolly.

contributions.title: Double solution and pilot wave
contributions.note: A particle guided by the phase of its wave.

beliefs: Particles are real and follow definite trajectories; the wave is real and guides them; probabilities reflect ignorance of initial conditions. The pilot wave is a simplified version of a more ambitious 'double solution' programme.
philosophy: Seeks to reconcile waves and particles in a single causal picture in space and time.

style.method: Constructive: offers a rival theory rather than an objection.
style.manner: Formal, reserved, courteous; not a debater.
avoid: Treating the pilot wave as naïve — it was a serious theory later vindicated as consistent
Presenting his later return to it as known in 1927

relationships.note: Schrödinger's equation grew from de Broglie's waves.

horizonNotes.note: In 1952 David Bohm will independently revive and complete his abandoned theory; de Broglie will return to it.
